title: test(types,plugin-list): drop the retired `navigation.view` authorings from the contract twins, and measure that the tombstone pin is not writable yet
body:
Fixes #9667

Clause-②: no — nothing published moves. Every source file in this diff is a
test under `packages/*/src/__tests__/`, plus one `.changeset/*.md` with EMPTY
frontmatter. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` reads the working tree
and prints `4 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change
declares 1 changeset(s)` with `Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter`. No
accept set is relaxed and no key on a published payload moves. (The seat's claim
comment carries `Seat:` / `Session:` / `Thread-read:` and no `Clause-②:` line,
so this one is written rather than copied.)

## What moved the contract

`objectstack-ai/objectstack` PR objectstack#18619 (card objectstack#16885,
director decision batch #126 item 4) retired `NavigationConfigSchema`'s `view`
slot as an ADR-0049 tombstone and merged 2026-09-17.

Re-taken on this branch's base rather than relayed. `git merge-base
--is-ancestor 3d8779d6c5 HEAD` in the sibling `objectstack` checkout exits **0**
— an is-ancestor answer is self-certifying and needs no control leg, unlike a
non-ancestor answer on a shallow checkout. That commit's subject is
`feat(spec)!: retire ListViewSchema.navigation.view, the detail-view binding
nothing ever resolved`, and the schema there now reads
`view: retiredKey(NAVIGATION_VIEW_RETIRED)`. ⚠️ The subject's trailing
PR-number parenthetical is dropped from that quote deliberately: a bare number
sitting next to that verb is exactly what GitHub's close-keyword parser matches,
and backticks do not protect it — that parser reads keyword-then-reference and
does not read sentences.

⭐ **The tombstone's exact shape is what the rest of this PR turns on.**
`retiredKey` is `z.never({ error: ... }).optional()`. So the key stays IN the
object shape — `keyof` still yields `view` — and only its authoring type
collapses from `string OR undefined` to `undefined`. That is why the gate's
diagnostic is `TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'undefined'` and
⛔ not an unknown-property error, and it is why `SpecDeclaredKeys` in the parity
file still lists `view` after this change. **DECLARED and WRITABLE are two
different facts.** Dropping `view` from that alias would redden
`_KeysAreExactlyTheSpecSix` against both the installed spec and spec main; a
comment on the alias now says so, because that line is the one most likely to be
"tidied" wrongly by the next reader.

## Per-site before and after

| site | before | after | in the gate's six? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| parity, mode-less case | `{ view: 'summary_view' }` | `{ preventNavigation: true }` | yes |
| parity, three schema sites (grid / view / named) | `{ navigation: { view: 'summary_view' } }` | `{ navigation: { preventNavigation: true } }` | yes |
| parity, every-spec-key case | six members incl. `view` | five members, `view` deliberately absent | yes |
| parity, docblock | taught `{ view: 'summary_view' }` as legal authored metadata | records the retirement and the DECLARED-vs-WRITABLE reading | not a diagnostic |
| `gantt-declared-keys`, un-annotated `good` literal | `{ mode: 'page' as const, view: 'task_detail', openNewTab: false }` | `{ mode: 'page' as const, openNewTab: false }` | **no** |
| `gantt-declared-keys`, annotated `ObjectGanttSchemaTS` literal | `{ mode: 'page', view: 'task_detail', openNewTab: false }` | `{ mode: 'page', openNewTab: false }` | yes |
| `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779`, `ACCEPTED` fixture | `{ mode: 'drawer', view: 'summary_view' }` | `{ mode: 'drawer', size: 'lg' }` | **no** |
| `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779`, three `safeParse` legs | authored `{ view: 'summary_view' }` and asserted it is ACCEPTED | `{ preventNavigation: true }` | **no — and not in the dispatch's enumeration either** |
| `ListView.ganttNavigationForward-7334`, authoring | `{ mode: 'split', view: 'leave_summary', size: 'lg' }` | `{ mode: 'split', size: 'lg' }` | **no** |
| `ListView.ganttNavigationForward-7334`, assertion | `toEqual({ mode: 'split', view: 'leave_summary', size: 'lg' })` | `toEqual({ mode: 'split', size: 'lg' })` | **no** |

⛔ **No case was weakened into vacuity.** Every repaired site keeps at least one
non-`mode` member, so each still measures what it measured before: mode-lessness
is now carried by `preventNavigation`, the gantt legs keep `mode` + `openNewTab`,
and the ListView forwarding case keeps `size` so it still proves the WHOLE
authored block is forwarded rather than a mode-only projection. ⛔ The parity
file's premise — `Equal` of `ViewNavigationConfig` and `NavigationConfig` — is
untouched, as are the four per-interface equality pins and the
`_KeysAreExactlyTheSpecSix` alias.

**Controls re-taken on this base, ⛔ not relayed.** `ViewNavigationConfig`
occurs on **20** lines of the parity file; the fabricated token the card names
occurs on **0**. Both matched the card. Every repaired site keeps a still-live
key, which is the per-site control the dispatch asked for: the file would go red
if the spec had narrowed rather than tombstoned.

## Why each out-of-the-six site is out, and ⭐ one correction to the dispatch

- **`gantt-declared-keys` un-annotated leg** — `const good = { ... }` has no type
  annotation and is handed to `safeParse`, which takes `unknown`. No
  excess/incompatible-property check has anything to fire against. As the
  dispatch read it.
- **`object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779` `ACCEPTED`** — ⭐ **this is the finding
  the dispatch asked for, and it is NOT the same shape as the un-annotated gantt
  leg.** That site IS annotated. Its annotation is a `Record` keyed by the
  mirrored-key union with **`unknown`** as the value type, so the annotation
  admits any object and never reaches `ViewNavigationConfig`. There is a second,
  independent erasure on the same fixture: the one place it does reach a typed
  literal re-casts it, to a `Record` of the same keys with `never` values. ⇒ two
  erasures, neither of them "un-annotated". The site was invisible to `tsc`, ⛔
  not cleared by it. A comment at the fixture now records this.
- **`plugin-list` — ⭐ THE CORRECTION.** The dispatch reads these two lines as
  absent from the six *only* because `@object-ui/plugin-list#type-check` never
  ran behind the fail-fast. Measured on this branch, that is **not the whole
  reason**: they would not have appeared even if it had run. The harness
  signature is `viewSchema(schema: RECORD_OF_STRING_TO_ANY)` — spelled in words
  because GitHub eats angle-bracket-shaped fragments — so the literal is checked
  against a value type of `any` and no property check fires. Two legs, run
  behind the shared verify lock, direction predicted before running:

  | leg | mutation | predicted | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list run type-check` |
  |:--|:--|:--|:--|
  | SUBJECT | `mode: 'split'` becomes `mode: 99999` at the very site | no diagnostic | **exit 0**, zero diagnostics |
  | LIT CONTROL | `const _tsSeesThisFile: number = 'nope';` added to the same file | reddens | **exit 2**, `TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'` |

  The control is what makes the subject leg readable: `tsc` demonstrably
  compiles that file, so leg A's silence is about the SITE, not about the file
  or the program. Both legs restored from `HEAD` and the restore verified by
  blob hash against `git rev-parse HEAD:PATH`, ⛔ not by a trap's exit code.

  ⇒ repairing the two `plugin-list` lines is still right — they teach a retired
  key and the assertion states a false claim about the contract — but it does
  ⛔ **not** move `Spec Main Shape Gate`. Fixing `packages/types` alone would
  still have cost a cycle, for the fail-fast reason the dispatch gives; this
  correction narrows what the NEXT cycle would have printed, it does not reverse
  the dispatch's instruction.

- **`object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779` `safeParse` legs — a site the enumeration
  did not carry.** Three assertions in that file authored `{ view:
  'summary_view' }` into `NavigationConfigSchema.safeParse` and asserted it is
  ACCEPTED, including a `toEqual` round-trip. `safeParse` takes `unknown`, so
  `tsc` never saw them and the gate could never print them — but a tombstoned
  key REFUSES at the parse, so on a spec carrying the retirement those three go
  red at **runtime**, in this package's own `pnpm test`. Different instrument,
  same defect, same file face. They are repaired here and called out rather than
  left for the dependency bump to discover.

## Half B — the tombstone pin, MEASURED and NOT WRITABLE

The card's second half asks the twin to assert the key is REFUSED. This
repository's convention for that is an `@ts-expect-error` directive over the
authored key, the shape `action-callback-retired-7068` uses in the same
directory, beside a still-live sibling read with no directive as its lit
control.

It was written and run, ⛔ not assumed. This package resolves
`@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, whose `NavigationConfigSchema` still declares
`view: z.ZodOptional OF z.ZodString`. With the directive in place:

```
src/__tests__/view-navigation-config-spec-parity.test.ts(200,7): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL  @object-ui/types@17.6.0 type-check
Exit status 2
```

That was the run's only diagnostic — which is also the confirmation that half A
compiles clean underneath it. ⇒ an `@ts-expect-error` is an assertion that
something FAILS, so it is red in exactly the world where the tombstone has not
arrived. The probe was removed; the pin is **owed**, on this same file, the day
this package's `@objectstack/spec` dependency moves onto a version carrying the
retirement.

⛔ It is not written here in a disabled, commented-out or version-conditional
form: a pin that passes on both sides of the contract it guards is the phantom
check this file exists to prevent. The debt is recorded in two places a future
reader will actually open — a section of the parity file's docblock, beside
where the pin goes, and the changeset body. Neither records a version number for
the claim to go stale against; both name the one command that re-derives it.

## Deliberately untouched

- `packages/react/src/hooks/__tests__/useNavigationOverlay.modeDefault.test.tsx`
  and `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridNavigationMembers-8071.test.tsx` —
  PR objectui#9936 inverted these two pins and kept their authored fixtures on
  purpose. objectui#9874, the card that owns them, is `needs-user-decision`. A
  dev does not edit the fixtures an open decision card is about. Not addressed
  here; objectui#9874 remains open and owns them.
- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` — the published docblock teaching the retired
  key. Out of scope: objectui#9938 owns it and remains open. ⚠️ The docblock
  inside the parity test IS repaired, because it sits in a file this PR rewrites
  and leaving it teaching the key while the code below stops using it is the
  contradiction this family is about.

## Tests

Every heavy run serialized behind `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

| run | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-list^...' run build` (dependency closure — `plugin-list`'s type-check reads sibling `dist` typings and cannot resolve them unbuilt) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list run type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the four touched files | `Test Files 4 passed (4)` · `Tests 239 passed (239)` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ packages/plugin-list/` | `Test Files 288 passed` · `Tests 5813 passed` after the repair below |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | exit 0, 8053 tracked text files scanned |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | exit 0, `0 new citation(s)` |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` · `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` · `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the four files | 4 files linted, **0 errors**, 5 warnings — all `no-explicit-any` on pre-existing harness lines this PR does not touch |

Exit codes were captured by redirecting to a file first and reading `$?` before
any pipe, never across one.

⭐ **The full-package run caught a real defect in this PR's own prose, and it is
worth recording.** The first draft of the parity docblock cited a sibling
retirement pin by name — and that pin asserts its own retired spelling appears
**nowhere** in the tracked tree, by `git grep`. The citation reddened it. The
citation was changed; the two files were re-run green. A test file's prose is
inside other tests' denominators, which is not obvious until it bites.

### ⚠️ Scope of the local reading, and what it does NOT prove

- **A green local type-check does NOT prove the gate goes green.** This package
  resolves `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, where `navigation.view` still exists and
  an authored name still compiles. The local runs prove the repair does not
  break anything against the INSTALLED spec; the `Spec Main Shape Gate` re-run
  on objectui#9877, which compiles against a spec built from objectstack `main`,
  is the only reading that answers whether the six diagnostics are gone.
- **The lint run is a declared narrowing, with its three pieces of evidence.**
  The repo-wide scan (`pnpm lint`) is CI's run. ① The universe is read from
  `eslint.config.js` itself, whose test-file blocks match `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`
  and `**/__tests__/**/*.{ts,tsx}`. ② The file count is read from
  `--format json`: 4 files. ③ Type-aware linting is **not** enabled — that
  config declares no `project` or `projectService` parser option — so this diff
  cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain.
- **`Governed Surface Queue Guard`** — this diff touches no governed surface:
  four test files and one changeset, no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`,
  `skills/**` or `docs/adr/**`.
- CI beyond the runs above has not converged at the time of writing; its status
  is `in_progress` and it is not waited on here.

## Reverse verification

⛔ None is claimed for half A, and the reason is stated rather than skipped: the
repair is a DELETION of authorings whose failure mode only exists on a spec this
checkout cannot resolve. Deleting the repair reproduces the base, and on
17.4.0 the base is green — so a mutation leg here would be green on both sides
and would prove nothing. The two discriminating measurements this PR does carry
are the half-B TS2578 reading and the `plugin-list` subject/control pair above,
both of which separate the two worlds they are about.
